subject: math
title: One-Step Equations: x + p = q and px = q
seo_title: Grade 6 One-Step Equations Worksheets: Solve x + p = q and px = q with Decimals and Fractions
standard_text: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 one-step equations worksheets: check solutions by substituting, solve x + p = q and px = q with whole numbers, decimals and fractions, use tape diagrams and balances, and write equations for word problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Undo the operation, and do the same to both sides: subtract to undo adding, divide to undo multiplying.
key_sub: x + 5 = 12, so x = 12 − 5 = 7 (not 17). 4x = 10, so x = 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. Check by substituting: 4 × 2.5 = 10.
body_html:
What does it mean to solve an equation?

An equation says two amounts are equal, like x + 5 = 12. A solution is a value of x that makes it true. To check a number, substitute it for x: 7 + 5 = 12 is true, so 7 is the solution.

To solve, get x alone with the inverse operation, and do the same thing to both sides so they stay equal.

The equationUndo it byExample
x + p = qsubtracting p from both sidesx + 5 = 12, so x = 12 − 5 = 7
px = qdividing both sides by p4x = 10, so x = 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5

A balance shows why it works

Solve x + p = q

Example

Solve x + 2.5 = 8.1.

2.5 is added to x, so subtract 2.5 from both sides: x = 8.1 − 2.5 = 5.6. Check: 5.6 + 2.5 = 8.1.

Answer: x = 5.6

Solve px = q

4x means 4 × x. A tape diagram shows 4 equal parts that make 10.

Example

Solve 34x = 6.

Divide both sides by 34. Dividing by 34 is the same as multiplying by 43: x = 6 × 43 = 8. Check: 34 × 8 = 6.

Answer: x = 8

Word problems

Choose a letter for the unknown. Write an equation that tells the story, solve it, and check the answer in the story.

Example

5 notebooks cost $8.75. How much does 1 notebook cost?

Let n be the cost of 1 notebook. 5n = 8.75, so n = 8.75 ÷ 5 = 1.75. Check: 5 × $1.75 = $8.75.

Answer: $1.75

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
x + 5 = 12, so x = 17Do the opposite: subtract 5. x = 7
4x = 2, so x = 2 (4 ÷ 2)Divide the other side by 4: x = 2 ÷ 4 = 12
34x = 6, so x = 4 12 (6 × 34)Divide by 34: 6 × 43 = 8
0.5x = 4.5, so x = 2.25Divide by 0.5: x = 9. Dividing by a number less than 1 makes it bigger
“5 times the cost” written as x + 5“Times” means multiply: 5x
Not checkingSubstitute the answer back into the equation

faq.q: How do you solve a one-step equation?
faq.a: Use the inverse operation to get the variable alone, and do it to both sides. Subtract to undo adding (x + 5 = 12, so x = 7), and divide to undo multiplying (4x = 10, so x = 2.5).

faq.q: How do you check if a number is a solution of an equation?
faq.a: Substitute the number for the variable and see if both sides are equal. 7 is a solution of x + 5 = 12 because 7 + 5 = 12.

faq.q: How do you solve an equation with a fraction, like 3/4 x = 6?
faq.a: Divide both sides by 3/4, which is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 4/3. 6 × 4/3 = 8, so x = 8.

faq.q: What one-step equations do 6th graders learn?
faq.a: In Grade 6 (Common Core 6.EE.B.7), students solve equations like x + p = q and px = q with whole numbers, decimals and fractions, and write them for word problems.

sets.title: Is it a solution? Substitute and check

items.q: Which value of x is a solution of x + 5 = 12?
items.e: Substitute 7 for x: 7 + 5 = 12 is true. If x = 17, then 17 + 5 = 22, not 12.

items.q: Which number makes 38 + x = 91 true?
items.e: Substitute 53 for x: 53 + 38 = 91 is true. If x = 129, then 129 + 38 = 167, not 91.

items.q: Which value of x makes x + 2.5 = 8.1 true?
items.e: Substitute 5.6 for x: 5.6 + 2.5 = 8.1 is true. If x = 10.6, then 10.6 + 2.5 = 13.1, not 8.1.

items.q: Which number is a solution of 34 = x + 14?
items.e: Substitute 12 for x: 12 + 14 = 34 is true. If x = 1, then 1 + 14 = 1 14, not 34.

items.q: Which value of x is a solution of 7x = 56?
items.e: Substitute 8 for x: 7 × 8 = 56 is true. If x = 392, then 7 × 392 = 2,744, not 56.

items.q: Which number makes 6x = 3 true?
items.e: Substitute 12 for x: 6 × 12 = 3 is true. If x = 18, then 6 × 18 = 108, not 3.

items.q: Which value of x makes 0.5x = 4.5 true?
items.e: Substitute 9 for x: 0.5 × 9 = 4.5 is true. If x = 2.25, then 0.5 × 2.25 = 1.125, not 4.5.

items.q: Which number is a solution of 8 = 23x?
items.e: Substitute 12 for x: 23 × 12 = 8 is true. If x = 5 13, then 23 × 5 13 = 3 59, not 8.

items.q: Which equation has x = 6 as a solution?
items.e: Substitute 6 for x in each equation. 5 × 6 = 30, so 5x = 30 is true. In 5x = 11, 5 × 6 = 30, not 11. Remember: 5x means 5 times x.

items.q: Which equation has x = 9 as a solution?
items.e: Substitute 9 for x in each equation. 9 + 4 = 13, so x + 4 = 13 is true. In 4x = 13, 4 × 9 = 36, not 13.

items.q: Which equation has x = 12 as a solution?
items.e: Substitute 12 for x in each equation. 3 × 12 = 36, so 3x = 36 is true. In 3x = 15, 3 × 12 = 36, not 15. Remember: 3x means 3 times x.

items.q: Which equation has x = 1.5 as a solution?
items.e: Substitute 1.5 for x in each equation. 1.5 + 4 = 5.5, so x + 4 = 5.5 is true. In 4x = 5.5, 4 × 1.5 = 6, not 5.5.

items.q: Which equation has x = 12 as a solution?
c: x + 12 = 6 12
items.e: Substitute 12 for x in each equation. 6 × 12 = 3, so 6x = 3 is true. In 6x = 6 12, 6 × 12 = 3, not 6 12. Remember: 6x means 6 times x.

items.q: Which equation has x = 8 as a solution?
items.e: Substitute 8 for x in each equation. 8 + 7 = 15, so x + 7 = 15 is true. In 7x = 15, 7 × 8 = 56, not 15.

items.q: Is 14 a solution of x + 9 = 23?
items.e: Substitute 14 for x: 14 + 9 = 23. Both sides are equal, so 14 is a solution.

items.q: Is 144 a solution of 4x = 36?
items.e: Substitute 144 for x: 4 × 144 = 576, not 36, so it is not a solution. The solution is 9, because 4 × 9 = 36.

items.q: Is 5.1 a solution of x + 1.6 = 3.5?
items.e: Substitute 5.1 for x: 5.1 + 1.6 = 6.7, not 3.5, so it is not a solution. The solution is 1.9, because 1.9 + 1.6 = 3.5.

items.q: Is 45 a solution of 5x = 4?
items.e: Substitute 45 for x: 5 × 45 = 4. Both sides are equal, so 45 is a solution.

items.q: Is 4 12 a solution of 34x = 6?
items.e: Substitute 4 12 for x: 34 × 4 12 = 3 38, not 6, so it is not a solution. The solution is 8, because 34 × 8 = 6.

items.q: Is 175 a solution of x + 125 = 300?
items.e: Substitute 175 for x: 175 + 125 = 300. Both sides are equal, so 175 is a solution.

sets.title: Solve x + p = q (subtract to undo adding)

items.e: Subtract 8 from both sides: x = 12 − 8 = 4. Check: 4 + 8 = 12. Not 20: that adds 8 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: What is the value of x in 16 + x = 40?
items.e: Subtract 16 from both sides: x = 40 − 16 = 24. Check: 24 + 16 = 40. Not 56: that adds 16 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Solve for x: x + 68 = 119
items.e: Subtract 68 from both sides: x = 119 − 68 = 51. Check: 51 + 68 = 119. Not 187: that adds 68 instead of subtracting it.
Subtract 306 from both sides: x = 700 − 306 = 394. Check: 394 + 306 = 700. Not 1,006: that adds 306 instead of subtracting it.
Subtract 990 from both sides: x = 1,500 − 990 = 510. Check: 510 + 990 = 1,500. Not 2,490: that adds 990 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: What is the value of x in x − 12 = 29?
items.e: Add 12 to both sides: x = 29 + 12 = 41. Check: 41 − 12 = 29. Not 17: that subtracts 12 instead of adding it.

items.q: Solve for x: x + 2.2 = 7.1
items.e: Subtract 2.2 from both sides: x = 7.1 − 2.2 = 4.9. Check: 4.9 + 2.2 = 7.1. Not 9.3: that adds 2.2 instead of subtracting it.
Subtract 0.55 from both sides: x = 6 − 0.55 = 5.45. Check: 5.45 + 0.55 = 6. Not 6.55: that adds 0.55 instead of subtracting it.
Subtract 6.5 from both sides: x = 12.86 − 6.5 = 6.36. Check: 6.36 + 6.5 = 12.86. Not 19.36: that adds 6.5 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: What is the value of x in x + 1.13 = 5.5?
items.e: Subtract 1.13 from both sides: x = 5.5 − 1.13 = 4.37. Check: 4.37 + 1.13 = 5.5. Not 6.63: that adds 1.13 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Solve for x: 2 = x + 0.7
items.e: Subtract 0.7 from both sides: x = 2 − 0.7 = 1.3. Check: 1.3 + 0.7 = 2. Not 2.7: that adds 0.7 instead of subtracting it.
Add 3.8 to both sides: x = 4.56 + 3.8 = 8.36. Check: 8.36 − 3.8 = 4.56. Not 0.76: that subtracts 3.8 instead of adding it.
Subtract 4.3 from both sides: x = 16 − 4.3 = 11.7. Check: 11.7 + 4.3 = 16. Not 20.3: that adds 4.3 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: What is the value of x in x + 14 = 34?
items.e: Subtract 14 from both sides: x = 34 − 14 = 12. Check: 12 + 14 = 34. Not 1: that adds 14 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Solve for x: 25 + x = 1
items.e: Subtract 25 from both sides: x = 1 − 25 = 35. Check: 35 + 25 = 1. Not 1 25: that adds 25 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Find x: x + 13 = 56
items.e: Subtract 13 from both sides: x = 56 − 13 = 12. Check: 12 + 13 = 56. Not 1 16: that adds 13 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Solve 78 = x + 38.
items.e: Subtract 38 from both sides: x = 78 − 38 = 12. Check: 12 + 38 = 78. Not 1 14: that adds 38 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: What is the value of x in x + 1 12 = 4?
items.e: Subtract 1 12 from both sides: x = 4 − 1 12 = 2 12. Check: 2 12 + 1 12 = 4. Not 5 12: that adds 1 12 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Solve for x: 23 + x = 3 14
items.e: Subtract 23 from both sides: x = 3 14 − 23 = 2 712. Check: 2 712 + 23 = 3 14. Not 3 1112: that adds 23 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Find x: x + 1 14 = 3 56
items.e: Subtract 1 14 from both sides: x = 3 56 − 1 14 = 2 712. Check: 2 712 + 1 14 = 3 56. Not 5 112: that adds 1 14 instead of subtracting it.

sets.title: Solve px = q (divide to undo multiplying)

items.q: Solve 9x = 54.
items.e: Divide both sides by 9: x = 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Check: 9 × 6 = 54. Not 486: that multiplies by 9 instead of dividing by 9.

items.q: What is the value of x in 9x = 126?
items.e: Divide both sides by 9: x = 126 ÷ 9 = 14. Check: 9 × 14 = 126. Not 1,134: that multiplies by 9 instead of dividing by 9.

items.q: Solve for x: 12x = 252
items.e: Divide both sides by 12: x = 252 ÷ 12 = 21. Check: 12 × 21 = 252. Not 3,024: that multiplies by 12 instead of dividing by 12.
Divide both sides by 25: x = 650 ÷ 25 = 26. Check: 25 × 26 = 650. Not 16,250: that multiplies by 25 instead of dividing by 25.

items.q: Solve 4x = 2.
items.e: Divide both sides by 4: x = 2 ÷ 4 = 12. Check: 4 × 12 = 2. Not 8: that multiplies by 4 instead of dividing by 4.

items.q: What is the value of x in 15 = 6x?
items.e: Divide both sides by 6: x = 15 ÷ 6 = 2 12. Check: 6 × 2 12 = 15. Not 90: that multiplies by 6 instead of dividing by 6.

items.q: Solve for x: 8x = 6
items.e: Divide both sides by 8: x = 6 ÷ 8 = 34. Check: 8 × 34 = 6. Not 48: that multiplies by 8 instead of dividing by 8.
Divide both sides by 0.5: x = 4.5 ÷ 0.5 = 9. Check: 0.5 × 9 = 4.5. Not 2.25: that multiplies by 0.5 instead of dividing by 0.5.
Divide both sides by 1.2: x = 6 ÷ 1.2 = 5. Check: 1.2 × 5 = 6. Not 7.2: that multiplies by 1.2 instead of dividing by 1.2.

items.q: What is the value of x in 9.6 = 4x?
items.e: Divide both sides by 4: x = 9.6 ÷ 4 = 2.4. Check: 4 × 2.4 = 9.6. Not 38.4: that multiplies by 4 instead of dividing by 4.

items.q: Solve for x: 0.25x = 3
items.e: Divide both sides by 0.25: x = 3 ÷ 0.25 = 12. Check: 0.25 × 12 = 3. Not 0.75: that multiplies by 0.25 instead of dividing by 0.25.
Divide both sides by 3: x = 0.42 ÷ 3 = 0.14. Check: 3 × 0.14 = 0.42. Not 1.26: that multiplies by 3 instead of dividing by 3.
Divide both sides by 2.5: x = 11.25 ÷ 2.5 = 4.5. Check: 2.5 × 4.5 = 11.25. Not 28.125: that multiplies by 2.5 instead of dividing by 2.5.

items.q: What is the value of x in 34x = 6?
items.e: Divide both sides by 34, which is the same as multiplying by 43: x = 6 × 43 = 8. Check: 34 × 8 = 6. Not 4 12: that multiplies by 34 instead of dividing by 34.

items.q: Solve for x: 23x = 10
items.e: Divide both sides by 23, which is the same as multiplying by 32: x = 10 × 32 = 15. Check: 23 × 15 = 10. Not 6 23: that multiplies by 23 instead of dividing by 23.

items.q: Find x: 7 = 12x
items.e: Divide both sides by 12, which is the same as multiplying by 2: x = 7 × 2 = 14. Check: 12 × 14 = 7. Not 3 12: that multiplies by 12 instead of dividing by 12.

items.q: Solve 15x = 34.
items.e: Divide both sides by 15, which is the same as multiplying by 5: x = 34 × 5 = 3 34. Check: 15 × 3 34 = 34. Not 320: that multiplies by 15 instead of dividing by 15.

items.q: What is the value of x in 5x = 23?
items.e: Divide both sides by 5: x = 23 ÷ 5 = 215. Check: 5 × 215 = 23. Not 3 13: that multiplies by 5 instead of dividing by 5.

items.q: Solve for x: 25x = 415
items.e: Divide both sides by 25, which is the same as multiplying by 52: x = 415 × 52 = 23. Check: 25 × 23 = 415. Not 875: that multiplies by 25 instead of dividing by 25.

items.q: Find x: 916 = 38x
items.e: Divide both sides by 38, which is the same as multiplying by 83: x = 916 × 83 = 1 12. Check: 38 × 1 12 = 916. Not 27128: that multiplies by 38 instead of dividing by 38.

sets.title: Models and inverse operations: tape diagrams, balances and first steps

items.q: Which equation matches the tape diagram?
items.e: The parts x and 18 make the whole 45: x + 18 = 45. Not 18x = 45: the diagram shows two parts added together, not equal parts. So x = 27.

items.q: Which equation matches the tape diagram?
items.e: There are 5 equal parts, each x, and they make 35: 5x = 35. Not x + 5 = 35: the parts are equal, so this is multiplication. So x = 7.

items.q: Which equation matches the tape diagram?
items.e: The parts x and 2.5 make the whole 6.5: x + 2.5 = 6.5. Not 2.5x = 6.5: the diagram shows two parts added together, not equal parts. So x = 4.

items.q: Which equation matches the tape diagram?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts, each x, and they make 22: 4x = 22. Not x + 4 = 22: the parts are equal, so this is multiplication. So x = 5.5.

items.q: What is the value of x?
items.e: The diagram shows x + 27 = 63. Subtract 27 from both sides: x = 63 − 27 = 36. Not 90: that adds 27 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: What is the value of x?
items.e: The diagram shows 6x = 21. Divide both sides by 6: x = 21 ÷ 6 = 3.5. Not 126: that multiplies by 6 instead of dividing by 6.

items.q: The scale is balanced. Which equation does it show?
items.e: The left pan holds x and 7, and it balances 15: x + 7 = 15. The two sides are equal, so x = 8.

items.q: The scale is balanced. Which equation does it show?
items.e: The left pan holds 3 boxes, each x, so it is 3x. It balances 18: 3x = 18. So x = 6.

items.q: The scale is balanced. What is the value of x?
items.e: The scale shows 26 + x = 40. Take 26 off both pans to keep it balanced: x = 40 − 26 = 14. Not 66: that adds 26 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: The scale is balanced. What is the value of x?
items.e: The scale shows 4x = 30. Split both pans into 4 equal groups: x = 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5. Not 120: that multiplies by 4 instead of dividing by 4.

items.q: What is the best first step to solve x + 4.6 = 9?
items.e: 4.6 is added to x, so subtracting 4.6 undoes it. Subtract 4.6 from both sides: x = 9 − 4.6 = 4.4. Check: 4.4 + 4.6 = 9.

items.q: What is the best first step to solve 15 + x = 32?
items.e: 15 is added to x, so subtracting 15 undoes it. Subtract 15 from both sides: x = 32 − 15 = 17. Check: 17 + 15 = 32.

items.q: What is the best first step to solve 8x = 56?
items.e: x is multiplied by 8, so dividing by 8 undoes it. Divide both sides by 8: x = 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Check: 8 × 7 = 56.

items.q: What is the best first step to solve 0.4x = 2?
items.e: x is multiplied by 0.4, so dividing by 0.4 undoes it. Divide both sides by 0.4: x = 2 ÷ 0.4 = 5. Check: 0.4 × 5 = 2.

c: Multiply both sides by 52
Multiply both sides by 25
Subtract 25 from both sides

items.q: What is the best first step to solve x − 12 = 30?
items.e: 12 is subtracted from x, so adding 12 undoes it. Add 12 to both sides: x = 30 + 12 = 42. Check: 42 − 12 = 30.

items.q: Jack solved x + 9 = 23 and got x = 32. What mistake did he make?
c: He added 9 instead of subtracting it
items.e: Jack added 9 instead of subtracting it. Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 23 − 9 = 14. Check: 14 + 9 = 23.

items.q: Ruby solved 6x = 3 and got x = 2. What mistake did she make?
c: She divided 6 by 3 instead of 3 by 6
items.e: Ruby divided 6 by 3 instead of 3 by 6. Divide both sides by 6: x = 3 ÷ 6 = 12. Check: 6 × 12 = 3.

c: He subtracted 34 from 6
He multiplied by 34 instead of dividing by it
items.e: Owen multiplied by 34 instead of dividing by it. Divide both sides by 34, which is the same as multiplying by 43: x = 6 × 43 = 8. Check: 34 × 8 = 6.

items.q: Eli solved 0.5x = 4.5 and got x = 2.25. What mistake did he make?
c: He multiplied by 0.5 instead of dividing by it
items.e: Eli multiplied by 0.5 instead of dividing by it. Divide both sides by 0.5: x = 4.5 ÷ 0.5 = 9. Check: 0.5 × 9 = 4.5.

sets.title: Word problems: write an equation and solve

items.q: Omar is 13 years old. He is 4 years older than his sister. Let s be his sister’s age. Which equation can you use to find s?
items.e: s + 4 = 13 matches the story. Subtract 4 from both sides: s = 13 − 4 = 9. Not 4s = 13: the story adds, it does not multiply.

items.q: A book costs $12.50. That is 5 times the cost of a pen. Let p be the cost of the pen in dollars. Which equation can you use to find p?
items.e: 5p = 12.50 matches the story. Divide both sides by 5: p = 12.50 ÷ 5 = 2.50. Not p + 5 = 12.50: the story has equal groups, so it multiplies.

items.q: Sam rode his bike 3.5 miles before lunch. By the end of the day, he had ridden 9 miles in all. Let m be the miles he rode after lunch. Which equation can you use to find m?
items.e: m + 3.5 = 9 matches the story. Subtract 3.5 from both sides: m = 9 − 3.5 = 5.5. Not 3.5m = 9: the story adds, it does not multiply.

items.q: A recipe uses 34 cup of sugar for each batch of cookies. Ben used 6 cups of sugar. Let b be the number of batches. Which equation can you use to find b?
items.e: 34b = 6 matches the story. Divide both sides by 34, which is the same as multiplying by 43: b = 6 × 43 = 8. Not b + 34 = 6: the story has equal groups, so it multiplies.

items.q: 8 friends share the cost of a party equally. The party costs $96. Let d be the amount each friend pays in dollars. Which equation can you use to find d?
items.e: 8d = 96 matches the story. Divide both sides by 8: d = 96 ÷ 8 = 12. Not d + 8 = 96: the story has equal groups, so it multiplies.

items.q: A plant grew 2.4 cm this week. Now it is 15.1 cm tall. Let h be its height last week in centimeters. Which equation can you use to find h?
items.e: h + 2.4 = 15.1 matches the story. Subtract 2.4 from both sides: h = 15.1 − 2.4 = 12.7. Not 2.4h = 15.1: the story adds, it does not multiply.

items.q: Kai walks at 3 miles per hour. Let t be the number of hours it takes him to walk 7.5 miles. Which equation can you use to find t?
items.e: 3t = 7.5 matches the story. Divide both sides by 3: t = 7.5 ÷ 3 = 2.5. Not t + 3 = 7.5: the story has equal groups, so it multiplies.

items.q: Sofia has saved $38. She needs $65 for a jacket. Let m be how much more money she needs in dollars. Which equation can you use to find m?
items.e: 38 + m = 65 matches the story. Subtract 38 from both sides: m = 65 − 38 = 27. Not 38m = 65: the story adds, it does not multiply.

items.q: A movie ticket and a snack cost $15.25 together. The snack costs $4.50. How much does the ticket cost?
items.e: Equation: t + 4.50 = 15.25. Subtract 4.50 from both sides: t = 15.25 − 4.50 = 10.75. Answer: $10.75. Not $19.75: that adds 4.50 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Leo’s mother is 41 years old. She is 29 years older than Leo. How old is Leo?
items.e: Equation: a + 29 = 41. Subtract 29 from both sides: a = 41 − 29 = 12. Answer: 12 years old. Not 70 years old: that adds 29 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: A hiking trail is 8.6 km long. Maya has hiked 5.75 km so far. How many more kilometers does she have to hike?
items.e: Equation: k + 5.75 = 8.6. Subtract 5.75 from both sides: k = 8.6 − 5.75 = 2.85. Answer: 2.85 km. Not 14.35 km: that adds 5.75 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Each batch of pancakes needs 23 cup of milk. Noah has 4 cups of milk. How many batches can he make?
items.e: Equation: 23b = 4. Divide both sides by 23, which is the same as multiplying by 32: b = 4 × 32 = 6. Answer: 6 batches. Not 2 23 batches: that multiplies by 23 instead of dividing by 23.

items.q: 5 notebooks cost $8.75. Each notebook costs the same. How much does 1 notebook cost?
items.e: Equation: 5n = 8.75. Divide both sides by 5: n = 8.75 ÷ 5 = 1.75. Answer: $1.75. Not $43.75: that multiplies by 5 instead of dividing by 5.

items.q: A car drives at the same speed for 4 hours and goes 210 miles. How many miles per hour does it drive?
items.e: Equation: 4s = 210. Divide both sides by 4: s = 210 ÷ 4 = 52.5. Answer: 52.5 miles per hour. Not 840 miles per hour: that multiplies by 4 instead of dividing by 4.

items.q: Lily needs 5 12 feet of ribbon. She has 2 34 feet. How many more feet of ribbon does she need?
items.e: Equation: r + 2 34 = 5 12. Subtract 2 34 from both sides: r = 5 12 − 2 34 = 2 34. Answer: 2 34 feet. Not 8 14 feet: that adds 2 34 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: A bag of 6 apples weighs 2.7 pounds. The apples all weigh the same. How much does 1 apple weigh?
items.e: Equation: 6a = 2.7. Divide both sides by 6: a = 2.7 ÷ 6 = 0.45. Answer: 0.45 pounds. Not 16.2 pounds: that multiplies by 6 instead of dividing by 6.

items.q: 0.75 pound of cheese costs $6. What is the price for 1 pound?
items.e: Equation: 0.75c = 6. Divide both sides by 0.75: c = 6 ÷ 0.75 = 8. Answer: $8.00. Not $4.50: that multiplies by 0.75 instead of dividing by 0.75.

items.q: Mia’s grandfather is 72 years old. He is 6 times as old as Mia. How old is Mia?
items.e: Equation: 6a = 72. Divide both sides by 6: a = 72 ÷ 6 = 12. Answer: 12 years old. Not 432 years old: that multiplies by 6 instead of dividing by 6.

items.q: Zoe spent $27.40 at the store and has $18.65 left. How much money did she have before shopping?
items.e: Equation: m − 27.40 = 18.65. Add 27.40 to both sides: m = 18.65 + 27.40 = 46.05. Answer: $46.05. Not $35.05: that adds without carrying.

items.q: A water tank holds 1,500 gallons when full. It has 1,275 gallons in it now. How many more gallons will fill it?
items.e: Equation: g + 1,275 = 1,500. Subtract 1,275 from both sides: g = 1,500 − 1,275 = 225. Answer: 225 gallons. Not 2,775 gallons: that adds 1,275 instead of subtracting it.
